Tweet 1:
Most AI workflow projects don't fail because the model wasn't good enough. They fail because of the infrastructure around it.

Tweet 2:
1/ The demo trap: calling an API and returning text isn't a production system. Production means prompt versioning, token budget management, fallback chains, and output validation. The gap between "works in demo" and "works at 3 AM Tuesday" is where teams get surprised.

Tweet 3:
2/ No observability = black box. Every LLM workflow needs:
• Request/response logging with correlation IDs
• Latency tracking per provider and prompt
• Cost tracking per execution
• Alerting when output quality degrades

You can't debug under pressure without these.

Tweet 4:
3/ Vendor lock-in at the wrong layer. Tying business logic to one provider's SDK means you're one pricing change from a rewrite. We've unified nine providers — switching models is a config change, not a migration.

Tweet 5:
A production AI workflow has the same properties as any production system: observable, testable, degrades gracefully, debuggable at midnight without waking you up. The model is one component. Build the system around it.
